mainTopic: Light and severe טומאה for animals and humans, and which kinds of blood (שרצים, fish, human) are forbidden
overview: This amud keeps working through a ברייתא about טומאה and about which kinds of blood are forbidden to eat. First it explains why a dead animal can get the light טומאת אוכלין but a מת cannot. Nobody treats a human body as food, and in רב חנניא's case of נבלה covered with dough, a מת's טומאה breaks through any covering. Next it clarifies three lines of the ברייתא. שרצים have 'no טומאה' only in the sense that they give no טומאה by carrying. Fish and grasshoppers are 'entirely permitted' because they need no שחיטה. Birds have 'no כלאים' only in the sense that their feathers are not part of the clothing ban, as אביי explains. Then רב rules that eating blood of שרצים earns lashes, and רבי זירא explains that the lashes come from the שרץ ban, not the blood ban. רב also forbids collected fish blood, and the גמרא settles this with the ברייתא: blood with scales in it is permitted, and blood without scales is forbidden. Finally, רב ששת says human blood has not even a command to keep away from it. A ברייתא that calls it forbidden challenges him, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A human corpse cannot get food-impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation: a small piece of מת, even when added to other food to make an egg's worth, does not get טומאת אוכלין, because nobody treats a human body as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes a corpse: even if he completes it to the needed amount, it does not become impure with food-impurity, because his intention is cancelled out by the view of all people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the explanation it just gave for the ברייתא: a piece of נבלה smaller than a כזית can get טומאת אוכלין, but a piece of מת cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To count as food for טומאת אוכלין, something has to be treated as food. One person may plan to eat a piece of a human body, but every other person would never do that, so his plan does not count. That is why the ברייתא says a person has only the severe טומאה and not the light one.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; this comes to leave out a certain case
the impurity of food, a lighter kind of טומאה
his intention is cancelled out because all other people think differently
completes or fills up a needed amount

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a מת is less impure than a dead animal. A מת carries the most severe טומאה. The point is only that it cannot also get the lighter טומאת אוכלין, because it is not treated as food.

phrases.english: to exclude a corpse,
phrases.notes: He means a piece of a human corpse smaller than an olive, the same size as the נבלה case just discussed.

phrases.english: even though one completes it [to an egg-bulk] –
it does not become impure with the impurity of food,
because his intention is cancelled
by the view of all people.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵת, אַף עַל גַּב דִּמְמַלֵּיא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first explanation of the ברייתא, which began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: animal flesh is food, human flesh is not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a small piece of מת completed to an egg-bulk would get טומאת אוכלין like a piece of נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מת never gets טומאת אוכלין, because one person's intent to eat it is cancelled out by everyone else's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A piece of מת does not get טומאת אוכלין even when completed to an egg-bulk.

steps.title: רב חנניא's case: an olive-sized piece covered in dough
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא explains the ברייתא differently: even a full כזית of נבלה can get טומאת אוכלין, if it is covered with dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא said: You can even say it is a full olive-bulk. What case are we dealing with here? Where one covered it with dough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניא gives a different way to explain when a dead animal gets the light טומאה: a full כזית of נבלה that is wrapped in dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first explanation needed a piece smaller than a כזית. רב חנניא says that is not needed. Because the נבלה is covered with dough, it cannot touch anything and pass on טומאה by touching, so the food-impurity rule becomes relevant even for a full כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive-bulk, the amount of נבלה that gives off טומאה
what case are we dealing with here? (used to set up a specific case)
he covered it
dough

phrases.english: Rav Chananya said:
you may even say that it is an olive-bulk,
what are we dealing with here?
for example, where one covered it with dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנַנְיָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דְּהָוֵי כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different case to explain the same ברייתא, instead of the less-than-a-כזית case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the light טומאה could only apply to a piece smaller than a כזית.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can apply even to a full כזית, if it is covered with dough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית of נבלה covered with dough can get טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Then it should need to be made wet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חנניא: if this נבלה is being treated as regular food, it should need הכשר, being made wet, before it can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should also need הכשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חנניא's case. Regular food only becomes impure after it gets wet, so this covered נבלה should need that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known rule is that food cannot get טומאת אוכלין until it has been made wet (הכשר). If רב חנניא is treating the covered נבלה like ordinary food, then the ברייתא should have mentioned that it needs הכשר, and it did not.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)
making food ready to become impure, by getting it wet with certain liquids
it should need

phrases.english: If so, let it also require being made susceptible [by liquid]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חנניא's case from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנניא's case of a כזית of נבלה covered with dough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the covered נבלה is being treated as ordinary food, it should follow the ordinary food rule of needing הכשר.

steps.title: It still passes on impurity by carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the need for הכשר is only for regular food, which gives off no טומאה at all. This covered נבלה still makes a person impure by carrying it, so it does not need הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule is only for other foods, which pass on impurity neither by touching nor by carrying. But here, even though it does not pass on impurity by touching because it is covered with dough, it should at least pass on impurity by carrying, since he is carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חנניא. The covered נבלה is different from regular food, because it still gives off טומאה when carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary foods need הכשר because on their own they give off no טומאה, neither by touching nor by carrying. The dough stops the נבלה from passing on טומאה by touching. But anyone who carries it still becomes impure, so it keeps its strong status and does not need הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: these words apply (only to a certain case); this limits a rule
touching, one way טומאה is passed on
carrying, another way טומאה is passed on
granted that
at least

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the need for הכשר depends on whether the item gives off any טומאה at all, by touching or by carrying.

phrases.english: That applies to other foods,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא מְטַמּוּ לָא בְּמַגָּע וְלָא בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: which do not pass on impurity, neither by touching nor by carrying.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, נְהִי דְּלָא מְטַמֵּא בְּמַגָּע,
phrases.english: But here, granted that it does not pass on impurity by touching,
because it is covered with dough,
it should at least pass on impurity by carrying,
since he is carrying it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every food needs הכשר before it can get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only food that gives off no טומאה at all needs הכשר. The covered נבלה still makes a person impure by carrying, so it does not need הכשר.

steps.title: Covering does not help a corpse
steps.stepSummary: In רב חנניא's approach, a מת is excluded because covering it with dough does not stop its severe טומאה, which breaks through upward and downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes a corpse: even if he covered it with dough, it passes on severe impurity, because its impurity breaks through and goes up, and breaks through and goes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב חנניא's explanation by showing why the dough trick works for an animal but not for a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering a נבלה with dough blocks טומאה by touching, which leaves room for the lighter טומאת אוכלין. A מת's טומאה goes right through any covering (טומאה בוקעת), so it always stays at the severe level. That is why the ברייתא says a person has only the severe טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: severe impurity
impurity breaks through and goes up
breaks through and goes down

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the ברייתא. (1) A piece of נבלה smaller than a כזית gets טומאת אוכלין, but a מת does not, because no one treats a human body as food. (2) רב חנניא: a כזית of נבלה covered with dough gets טומאת אוכלין, and it needs no הכשר because it still passes on טומאה by carrying. A מת is different, because its טומאה breaks through any covering.

phrases.english: to exclude a corpse,
for even though one covered it with dough
it passes on a severe impurity,
because the impurity breaks through and goes up,
breaks through and goes down.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵת, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּחִיפָּהוּ בְּבָצֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חנניא's approach by explaining the ברייתא's exclusion of a person, matching step 1 in the first approach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רב חנניא's approach, a dead animal can get the light טומאה when covered with dough, but a מת cannot, because its severe טומאה breaks through any covering.

steps.title: Do creeping animals really have no impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא, which says blood of שרצים is left out because they have no טומאה. It asks: a שרץ does make things impure by touch!
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said creeping animals are left out because they have no impurity. But they do have impurity, since a dead שרץ makes things impure by touch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and right away challenges it. Everyone knows a dead שרץ gives off טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a reason why the blood of שרצים is not included in the ban on blood: 'they have no טומאה.' But a dead שרץ clearly makes things impure when it is touched, so that reason seems false.

keyTerms.meaning: Small creeping creatures, like mice and lizards
Ritual impurity
Touching; making something impure by contact

phrases.english: The Master said:
Creeping animals are excluded
since they do not have impurity.
And do they not?
A creeping animal makes things impure through touching!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new close reading of the ברייתא about forbidden blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that שרצים have no טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dead שרץ makes things impure by touch, so it plainly does have טומאה.

steps.title: No impurity by carrying
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a שרץ makes things impure by touch, but not by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שרץ does not make a person impure just by carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא meant. It was talking about the stronger kind of טומאה that comes through carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה makes a person impure even if he only carries it, without touching it. A שרץ lacks that stronger power. So 'no טומאה' means it does not have the stronger kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying; making a person impure by carrying something, even without touching it

phrases.english: Through carrying, it does not make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the ברייתא's words more specific
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No טומאה' sounded like no impurity at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means no טומאה through carrying.

steps.title: What does 'entirely permitted' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא leaves out the blood of fish and grasshoppers because they are 'entirely permitted.' The גמרא asks what that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said fish blood and grasshopper blood are left out because they are entirely permitted. What does 'entirely permitted' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and asks what one phrase means. This sets up the next steps, which test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish and grasshoppers do have some rules about eating, so 'entirely permitted' needs a clear meaning. The גמרא will test several ideas before choosing one.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish
Grasshoppers (kosher kinds of locust)
Entirely permitted

phrases.english: The Master said:
Excluded is the blood of fish
and the blood of grasshoppers
since it is entirely permitted.
What does "entirely permitted" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next reason given in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'entirely permitted' for fish and grasshoppers

steps.title: Not because their fat is permitted
steps.stepSummary: First idea: it means their fat is permitted. Rejected, because a חיה's fat is permitted, yet its blood is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it means their fat is allowed? No. A wild animal's fat is allowed, and still its blood is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'permitted fat' were the reason blood is allowed, then a חיה's blood would be allowed too. But a חיה's blood is forbidden, so permitted fat cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat. In a בהמה it is forbidden, but in a חיה it is allowed.
A wild animal, like a deer

phrases.english: If you say it means that its fat is permitted —
but look at a wild animal, whose fat is permitted
and yet its blood is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to the question in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'entirely permitted' means permitted fat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חיה has permitted fat but forbidden blood.

steps.title: Not because there is no גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: Second idea: it means they have no ban on גיד הנשה. Rejected, because birds have no גיד הנשה ban, yet their blood is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it means there is no ban on their sciatic nerve? No. A bird has no such ban, and still its blood is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning and rejects it the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird has no גיד הנשה ban, and its blood is still forbidden. So having no גיד הנשה ban cannot be what makes fish and grasshopper blood allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat
Bird

phrases.english: Rather, is it because they do not have
the prohibition of the sciatic nerve?
But look at a bird, which does not have
the prohibition of the sciatic nerve,
and yet its blood is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא: מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵית בְּהוּ אִיסּוּר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a second answer after the first one failed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'entirely permitted' means no גיד הנשה ban
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bird has no גיד הנשה ban but forbidden blood.

steps.title: It means no slaughter is needed
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: 'entirely permitted' means fish and grasshoppers do not need שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Entirely permitted' means they can be eaten without ritual slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the meaning that works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חיה and עוף both need שחיטה, and both have forbidden blood. Fish and grasshoppers need no שחיטה at all, and this is what sets them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher ritual slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: Fish and grasshopper blood is left out of the ban on blood because these creatures are permitted without שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rather, what does "entirely permitted" mean?
That it does not need slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that holds up after two ideas were rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Entirely permitted' means they need no שחיטה.

steps.title: Why the verse also says 'animal'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: if the פסוק said only עוף, one might limit the ban to animals that, like birds, have no כלאים. So the פסוק says בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: a bird has no כלאים, so the ban on blood covers only animals that also have no כלאים. That is why the verse says 'animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains why the פסוק names בהמה along with עוף. Without that word, one might think only creatures that are like birds in having no כלאים have forbidden blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixing of different kinds
Domesticated animal
The verse teaches; introduces a proof from the פסוק

phrases.english: The Master said:
Just as a bird has no prohibition of diverse kinds,
so too, the animal meant here is only one without diverse kinds —
therefore the verse says: "animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מָה עוֹף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word בהמה is needed so the ban on blood is not limited to creatures without כלאים, as a bird is.

steps.title: Which kind of כלאים do birds lack?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which כלאים the ברייתא had in mind when it said birds have no כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלאים of what kind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask which כלאים law the ברייתא from the last step was talking about. This question sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said birds are different because they have no כלאים. But there are several kinds of כלאים laws, so the גמרא needs to know which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of different kinds (animals, plants, or materials)
Of what? Which kind?

phrases.english: כלאים of what kind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which כלאים law the ברייתא meant when it said birds have no כלאים

steps.title: It cannot mean mating or plowing
steps.stepSummary: Mating and plowing cannot be meant, since a משנה says those rules apply to wild animals and birds too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means כלאים of mating and כלאים of plowing, but we learned in a משנה: wild animals and birds are just like them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא meant mating or plowing with two kinds together, then rejects that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה teaches that the bans on mating two species and plowing with two species apply to חיה and עוף just like בהמה. So birds do have these kinds of כלאים, and the ברייתא cannot mean them.

keyTerms.meaning: Mating two different species together
Plowing with two different species together
The same as them

phrases.english: If you say it means כלאים of mating
and כלאים of plowing,
but we learned: wild animals and birds are the same as them!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא קמא 54b. It means the mating and plowing rules for farm animals apply to these too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and knocks it down
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא meant mating or plowing כלאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה says birds are included in the mating and plowing bans, so birds do have that כלאים

steps.title: אביי: it means a bird's 'wool'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a bird's feathers are not included in the כלאים ban on clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: it means that for its wool, one is not liable for כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the real answer: the ברייתא meant the כלאים of clothing, which does not apply to a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on mixing wool and linen in clothing is only about sheep's wool. A bird's 'wool' (its feathers) mixed with linen is not forbidden, so in that sense birds have no כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Its wool (for a bird, its feathers)
One is not liable for it

steps.whatToRemember: Birds do have mating and plowing כלאים, but the clothing ban of wool and linen does not include their feathers.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
that for its wool one is not liable
phrases.notes: For a bird, its 'wool' means its feathers.

phrases.english: because of כלאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected idea with the correct meaning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means birds have no clothing כלאים: their feathers mixed with linen are not forbidden

steps.title: רב: blood of שרצים earns מלקות
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that eating an olive-size amount of the blood of שרצים earns lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: for the blood of שרצים, one gets lashes for an olive-size amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of רב about eating the blood of creeping creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of שרצים is not the regular blood that brings כרת. Still, רב says it is forbidden by a לאו, so eating a כזית earns מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Small creeping creatures
One receives lashes (מלקות)
An olive-size amount, the usual minimum for punishment in eating

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For the blood of creeping creatures, one gets lashes for an olive-size amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new discussion about blood of שרצים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a כזית of blood of שרצים is punished with מלקות

steps.title: A ברייתא says no liability for blood of שרצים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists blood of שרצים as forbidden but with no liability, which seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Blood of the spleen, heart, kidneys, and limbs: these are under a לאו. Blood of humans, and blood of שרצים and crawling things: forbidden, but one is not liable for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא that seems to say there is no punishment at all for blood of שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts organ blood under a לאו, but puts שרצים blood in a lower group: 'forbidden, but not liable.' That sounds like no מלקות, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, punished with lashes
Those who walk on two legs, meaning humans
Crawling things

phrases.english: They challenged:
Blood of the spleen, blood of the heart,
blood of the kidneys, blood of the limbs –
these are under a negative commandment.
Blood of those who walk on two legs,
blood of creeping and crawling creatures –
is forbidden, but one is not liable for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that blood of שרצים earns מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'not liable' for blood of שרצים, which seems to mean no punishment at all, not even lashes

steps.title: 'Not liable' means no כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא means no כרת, but there is still a לאו with lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not liable for it' mean? Not liable for כרת, but for a לאו one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the challenge by reading 'not liable' in the ברייתא more narrowly. The next step rejects this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not liable' only removes כרת. A לאו still applies, so מלקות are given, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating regular blood
A negative commandment, punished with lashes
Is liable

phrases.english: What does 'one is not liable for it' mean? Not liable for כרת,
but for a negative commandment, one is liable.
phrases.notes: The word is shortened in the text; the square brackets fill it in as אבל, 'but.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and defends רב
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrow reading of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not liable' meant no punishment at all
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not liable' means no כרת, but there is a לאו with lashes, matching רב

steps.title: The earlier answer about blood of שרצים fails for two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The answer that the ברייתא means 'no כרת but still a לאו' is rejected for two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, that would make this clause the same as the first clause. Second, a תנא removes blood of שרצים even from the לאו, since he teaches: 'Excluded is the blood of שרצים, because they do not have serious טומאה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 18 and gives two separate reasons why it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: the ברייתא's first clause already listed bloods that carry a לאו but no כרת, so the שרצים clause cannot mean the same thing again. Reason two: another teaching says blood of שרצים is not under the blood לאו at all. So the problem with רב's ruling from step 17 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
a regular Torah prohibition (punished with lashes, not כרת)
excludes, limits a law so it does not cover something
serious ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Reason two does not say blood of שרצים is permitted. It only says this blood does not fall under the special ban on blood.

phrases.english: One problem: that is the same as the first clause.
And furthermore, a תנא, even from the לאו
excludes it,
as he teaches: excluded is the blood of שרצים,
because they do not have serious טומאה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole answer that 'no liability' means 'no כרת but still a לאו'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It repeats the first clause, and another teaching removes blood of שרצים from the blood לאו altogether.

steps.title: Lashes come from the שרץ ban, not from the blood ban
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the lashes in רב's ruling come from the prohibition of eating a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: If they warned him because of שרץ, he gets lashes. If they warned him because of blood, he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a new way to fit רב's ruling with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of a שרץ counts as part of the שרץ, so eating it breaks the ban on eating a שרץ. It does not break the special ban on blood. So the ברייתא (no liability as blood) and רב (lashes) can both be true, as long as the warning names the right prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: they warned him (a warning is required before lashes)
he gets lashes
a small creeping creature that is forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: Blood of a שרץ: lashes come from the שרץ ban, not from the blood ban. The warning must name the שרץ ban.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one food can be forbidden under one ban and not another, and lashes depend on which ban the warning named.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
If they warned him because of the ban on שרץ, he gets lashes;
if because of the ban on blood, he does not get lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הִתְרוּ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 19 rejected the old one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits between two prohibitions: the שרץ ban versus the blood ban.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב gave lashes for breaking the blood ban, which the ברייתא denies.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's lashes are for the שרץ ban; the ברייתא only says there is no blood ban here.

steps.title: Fish blood gathered into a vessel is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that fish blood gathered into a vessel may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Fish blood that someone gathered is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling of רב about fish blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish blood is not part of the Torah's ban on blood. Even so, רב forbids it when it has been gathered by itself in a vessel, since then it is hard to tell it apart from forbidden blood.

keyTerms.meaning: fish blood
that he gathered it (into a vessel)
forbidden

phrases.english: Rav said:
Fish blood that someone gathered is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: דַּם דָּגִים שֶׁכִּינְּסוֹ – אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the שרצים discussion ended.

steps.title: A ברייתא permits fish blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says fish blood and grasshopper blood are permitted, even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Fish blood and grasshopper blood are permitted, even from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says fish blood is permitted without any condition. That seems to contradict רב, who forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: grasshoppers (kosher types of locust)
permitted
from the start, allowed in the first place

phrases.english: They objected:
Fish blood and grasshopper blood are permitted,
and even from the start!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: דַּם דָּגִים, דַּם חֲגָבִים – מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that gathered fish blood is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits fish blood with no condition, so how can רב forbid it?

steps.title: Gathered versus not gathered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means fish blood that was not gathered; רב means blood that was gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is about blood he did not gather. When רב spoke, he meant blood he did gather.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying רב and the ברייתא are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish blood that is still on the fish or mixed in the food is permitted. Only once it is gathered by itself does רב forbid it. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: that one (that teaching)
when he did not gather it

phrases.english: That one is about when he did not gather it;
when Rav spoke, he meant when he did gather it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא בְּשֶׁלֹּא כִּינְּסוֹ, כִּי קָא אָמַר רַב – בְּשֶׁכִּינְּסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: gathered blood versus blood that was not gathered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permits all fish blood, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only permits blood that was not gathered; רב forbids gathered blood.

steps.title: Human blood that was not gathered is permitted
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא means blood that was not gathered, its ban on human blood would also mean blood that was not gathered, yet such blood is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the matching case of humans, blood that was not gathered, is it forbidden? But a ברייתא teaches: Blood on a loaf of bread, he scrapes it off and eats the bread. Blood between the teeth, he sucks it and swallows it and does not worry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 23 using the human blood clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ברייתא forbids human blood. If the whole ברייתא is about blood that was not gathered, then it forbids human blood that was not gathered. But another ברייתא says blood between the teeth may be swallowed, so such human blood is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: the matching case
two-legged walkers, meaning humans
he scrapes it off
he sucks it
he does not need to worry

phrases.english: In the matching case of two-legged ones,
phrases.notes: He means humans, whose blood an earlier line of that same ברייתא forbids.

phrases.english: when he did not gather it, is it forbidden?
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: דָּם שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי כִּכָּר – גּוֹרְרוֹ וְאוֹכְלוֹ,
phrases.english: Blood on a loaf of bread: he scrapes it off and eats it;
blood between the teeth: he sucks it and swallows it
and does not worry!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְווֹתַהּ גַּבֵּי מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם – בְּשֶׁלֹּא כִּינְּסוֹ, מִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about blood that was not gathered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, its ban on human blood is also about blood that was not gathered, but such human blood, like blood between the teeth, is permitted.

steps.title: Scales make the difference for fish blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer. The ברייתא permits even collected fish blood when scales are in it. רב forbids it only when no scales are in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: when that ברייתא is taught, it is talking about blood that has scales in it. When רב said it is forbidden, he meant blood that has no scales in it.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 24 knocked down the earlier answer, so the גמרא offers a completely new way to settle the contradiction between רב and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is no longer 'collected or not collected.' Even collected fish blood is permitted when scales floating in it show it comes from a fish. Without scales, people might think it is animal blood, so רב forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: signals the old answer is dropped and a new one is given
A teaching of the תנאים; here it refers to the ברייתא
Fish scales

steps.whatToRemember: Fish blood collected in a vessel: permitted when scales show it is from a fish, forbidden (by רב) when there are no scales.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer replaces the 'collected vs. not collected' answer from step 23. Do not combine the two answers.

phrases.english: Rather:
when that baraita is taught,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 22 that permits fish blood and grasshopper blood.

phrases.english: it is where there are scales in it;
when Rav said it is forbidden,
it is where there are no scales in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 24 refuted the answer in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): scales present vs. no scales
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling depended on whether the blood was collected in a vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling depends on whether scales show it is fish blood.

steps.title: Human blood has no requirement to avoid it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that human blood carries not even a command to keep away from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: the blood of creatures that walk on two legs does not even carry a command to keep away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב ששת says human blood is not forbidden at any level, not even as a מצוה to stay away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some foods carry full lashes, some are 'forbidden but no punishment,' and some carry only a מצוה to keep away. רב ששת puts human blood below all of these. He says there is no command at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Those that walk on two legs: human beings
A command to keep away: the lightest level of avoidance

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
the blood of those that walk on two legs
does not even have a command to keep away from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: דַּם מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, human blood, which connects to the human blood question raised in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human blood carries no prohibition at all, not even a מצוה to keep away from it.

steps.title: A ברייתא says human blood is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists human blood among things that are 'forbidden, but one is not liable.' That clashes with רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: blood of the spleen, heart, kidneys, and limbs falls under a negative commandment. Human blood and the blood of creeping and crawling creatures is forbidden, but one is not punished for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת with a ברייתא that clearly calls human blood 'forbidden.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said human blood has no prohibition at all. The ברייתא says it is forbidden, just without punishment. 'Forbidden' and 'not even a command to avoid' cannot both be true.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment from the Torah
Spleen
Blood that stays inside the limbs
Creeping and crawling creatures
Forbidden, but there is no punishment for eating it

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
blood of the spleen, blood of the heart,
blood of the kidneys, blood of the limbs:
these are under a negative commandment.
Blood of those that walk on two legs,
blood of creeping and crawling creatures,
is forbidden, but one is not liable for it!
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making the word plural.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's statement in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that human blood has not even a command to keep away from it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls human blood 'forbidden,' which directly contradicts 'no command at all.'

steps.title: Starting to explain the ברייתא's 'forbidden'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer by limiting the case in which the ברייתא calls human blood forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the ברייתא teaches 'forbidden'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer for רב ששת. It is about to explain which kind of human blood the ברייתא means when it says 'forbidden.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'when it is taught' signal that the answer will narrow the ברייתא to a specific case. That way it no longer clashes with רב ששת. The answer is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: When it is taught: introduces a narrowing of what a ברייתא is talking about
Forbidden: here, the ברייתא's word that is being explained

phrases.english: When it is taught that it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. The גמרא completes it on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) of the ברייתא; continues in the following text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids all human blood, against רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's 'forbidden' applies only to a specific case, which the גמרא spells out on the next amud.
